The leader of the sponsoring country publicly threatened to impose 100% tariffs on goods from a major economy in a few months and hinted at restricting the export of aircraft parts, which may end the fragile trade truce.

The sponsoring country's ambassador to the rival economy previously revealed that the two countries were in the final stages of negotiations on a large-scale passenger aircraft sale, but the deal now faces uncertainty

The sponsoring country simultaneously stated that it will implement export controls on "any and all critical software". The relevant tariffs may take effect within a few weeks or earlier, depending on the follow-up actions of the other party.
Rival economies have officially begun to levy port fees on ships associated with the sponsoring country, which will be charged based on net tonnage and will increase year by year.
The financial chief of the sponsoring country said that the leaders of the two countries are still expected to meet in a third country in the fall to ease trade tensions.

The trade and finance chiefs of the sponsoring countries made a joint appearance for the first time, characterizing the rare earth export restrictions of rival economies as 'economic coercion' and threatening that the world will have to decouple from them.
Officials from the sponsoring country revealed that previously threatened measures such as 100% tariffs on the economy and export controls on key software are being drafted.

Leaders of the sponsoring countries signed an executive order to impose a 25% tariff on imported medium- and heavy-duty trucks, with partial exemptions for regional agreements, and a lower tax rate for passenger cars.

The leader of the sponsoring country announced the termination of all trade negotiations with a neighboring country because the local government of a neighboring country placed an advertisement that quoted the former president's criticism of tariffs, and accused the advertisement of forgery with the intention of interfering with judicial review.

The neighboring country's regional government responded by saying it would pause advertising in the sponsoring country to allow negotiations to resume, but ads would continue to air during major weekend events.

The financial and economic chief of the sponsoring country announced that it has reached a "framework" for a substantive trade agreement with its rival economy, which involves the other party's substantial increase in the purchase of agricultural products and assistance in the control of fentanyl precursor chemicals.
The initiating country and the rival economy reach a final agreement on a short video application transaction, which will be formally confirmed by the leaders of the two countries in a third country

Leaders of the sponsoring countries publicly stated that they would consider reducing tariffs on rival economies in exchange for controlling the export of fentanyl precursor chemicals, and for the first time clearly linked trade policy to anti-drug issues.

The first house of the sponsoring country's legislative body passed a resolution by a narrow majority to terminate the national emergency declaration based on the president's tariffs on a neighboring country. Several ruling party members defected, but the resolution was difficult to translate into law.

The highest judicial body of the sponsoring country is scheduled to hold a hearing on the legality of the president's implementation of global tariffs in accordance with the emergency authorization law in the near future, and the chief financial officer will attend the defense.

A small company that relies on imported fabrics became a direct victim of the trade war and was forced to repeatedly adjust pricing and lay off employees due to the sharp rise and fall of relevant tariffs in a few months.

The highest judicial body of the sponsoring country held a hearing on the legality of widespread tariffs. Many justices (including conservatives) expressed sharp doubts about the government's justification for the tax and worried that huge refunds would cause chaos if they lose the case.

The leaders of the sponsoring countries signed an executive order to implement tariff exemptions for dozens of foods that cannot be produced locally, such as coffee, bananas, beef, and cocoa, after rising grocery prices became a political issue.
The ruling party pushes to provide people with $2,000 tariff rebate checks to drum up support, even as the top judicial body reviews the tariff legal authority

The leader of the initiating country formally sent a letter to a neighboring country issuing a new tariff threat and ultimatum, requiring it to deliver the agreed volume of water in accordance with the cross-border water resources treaty obligations by a specified cutoff, otherwise additional tariffs will be imposed on its goods.
